provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The mechanism is: find each hollow square frame in the frame colour palette[5] on the background palette[0]. Then fill its background interior with a colour chosen by interior side length k = L-2. The generator writes gray + k, so k=3 gives palette[8], k=2 gives palette[7] and k=1 gives palette[6]. Frames are found as 4-connected components of the frame colour. A component is accepted when its bounding box is square, its side is 3 to 5, its cell count is 4*(L-1), and the border is all frame colour with an all-background interior. Every D4 transform maps a square frame to a square frame of the same size, and the fill depends only on size. So the same visible-coordinate rule applies under all D4 settings with no axis or direction specialisation; d4 is intentionally unused. Colour roles are fixed constants taken from the palette. As a defensive fallback, if a component is not one clean frame (for example two frames touching), the program scans its bounding box for exact L x L hollow-frame templates (L = 5, 4, 3) and fills each match. Frames at grid edges are handled because only the frame's own bounding box is used.
draft_notes.limitations: The program relies on the constructor domain: square frames of side 3, 4 or 5 in palette[5] on palette[0], with fill colours palette[6], palette[7], palette[8] (from the generator's gray + length - 2). Any other frame size is left unchanged, because the demonstrations define no colour for it. Demonstrations are not used to re-learn the table. The generator's overlap check uses a buffer of 1, so frames should never touch; the touching-frame fallback is untested defensive code. The generator sometimes silently drops a frame when its random placement overlaps (seen as two-frame scenes); this is harmless to the rule, and the program handles any number of frames. No contradictions between the fixtures and the rule were observed. Nothing has been run or tested.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Each hollow square frame in palette[5] on background palette[0] has its interior filled with a colour chosen by side length L. The constructor writes gray()+L-2, so L=3 gets palette[6], L=4 gets palette[7] and L=5 gets palette[8], assuming the palette is applied as a post-hoc permutation. The factory finds 4-connected FR components. It checks for a square bounding box, (H-2) in {1,2,3}, a cell count of 4(H-1), and an exact frame template. It then fills background interior cells with FILL[H-2]. Square frames are D4-invariant and the fill depends only on size, so the solver correctly works directly in visible coordinates without a wrapper.
evidence: Constructor: the line `output[...] = common.gray() + length - 2` maps sizes 5/4/3 to canonical colours 8/7/6. The factory's FILL = {1: palette[6], 2: palette[7], 3: palette[8]} indexed by H-2 matches this.

Constructor: `common.overlaps(..., 1)` in common.py requires a gap of at least one cell (`rows[i]+talls[i]+1 <= rows[j]`) on some axis, so placed frames never touch, even diagonally. Each FR component is therefore exactly one frame, and the touching-frame fallback is out of domain.
The fixtures (canonical, uncorrected) agree with the archived rule and the factory. Pair 3 has no 3x3 frame; pairs 1 and 2 demonstrate it.
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs and 8000 augmented checks.
The factory leaves d4 unused. This is legitimate because square frames and size-keyed fills are D4-invariant. There is no untransform, native-solve or retransform wrapper.
blocking_issues: Missing demonstration evidence for an arbitrary size-to-colour lookup. Under palette augmentation, the colour for each frame size (palette[6]/[7]/[8]) is an arbitrary association that can only be learned from a demonstration where that size is filled. The constructor silently drops frames on overlap (`if common.overlaps(...): continue`) very often. With the 5x5 frame uniformly placed in [0,7]^2, a 4x4 frame placed in [0,8]^2 conflicts with probability about (7.5/9)^2 ≈ 0.69. The 3x3 frame is dropped at a comparably high rate because it is checked against both frames. This matches the host's 624 unique inputs out of 1000, which points to many single-frame scenes. Rough estimate: with 3 demonstrations, P(no demo contains a 4x4 frame) ≈ 0.33 and P(query contains one) ≈ 0.31. So about 10% of episodes, plus a similar share for 3x3, require a query colour never shown. The supplied episode_evidence_checks do not list c0f76784, so these episodes are not rejected. The factory answers them correctly only because it hard-codes the palette lookup, which is unidentifiable from the episode.
nonblocking_limits: Frame dropping is far more frequent than the prior notes' 'sometimes' suggests: most scenes lose the 4x4 and/or 3x3 frame. This is constructor behaviour and harmless to rule correctness.

Correct fill colours assume the host applies the palette as a post-hoc colour permutation rather than via common.set_colors. With set_colors, gray()+k would be palette[5]+k. The passing augmented audit supports the post-hoc interpretation.
The touching-frame fallback in the factory cannot be reached under the constructor's spacing-1 overlap rule.
The fixed table ignores demonstrations. This is acceptable as specialisation of the genuine rule colours, provided the evidence check above is enforced.
required_context_checks: Add a c0f76784 episode check: for every frame side L in {3,4,5} present in any query input, require at least one demonstration whose output fills an L x L frame interior. Equivalently, the colour palette[L+3] must appear in some demonstration output inside a frame. Otherwise reject or resample the episode.
Confirm the palette is applied as a permutation after generation, so that gray()+k corresponds to palette[5+k].

draft_notes.host_review: Reviewed mechanism, evidence, limitations and checks. Shared bijective palette and horizontal-reflection-then-clockwise-rotation convention confirmed. All eight D4 indices audited, with d4=7 being the final loop index. Per-episode execution and context checks remain required. Added and regression-tested required query mapping evidence using only demonstration answers and query inputs, across all eight D4 transformations with nonidentity palette. Unseen mappings now reject the episode.
